test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 24 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: For a regular polygon, the sum of the interior angles is 200% more than the sum of its exterior angles. Each interior angle of the polygon measures x°. What is the value of x?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of **interior angles** = 3 × Sum of **exterior angles** (since 200% more means 100% + 200% = 300%).

(n − 2) × 180° = 3 × 360°

n − 2 = (3 × 360) ÷ 180 ⇒ n − 2 = 6 ⇒ n = 8 (**Octagon**).

Each **exterior angle** = 360° ÷ 8 = 45°.

Each **interior angle** (x) = 180° − 45° = 135°.

**∴ The correct answer is 135°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of **interior angles** = Sum of **exterior angles** + 200% of Sum of **exterior angles**.

**Formula Used:**

1. Sum of **interior angles** of an n-sided polygon = (n − 2) × 180°

2. Sum of **exterior angles** of any polygon = 360°

3. Each **interior angle** of a regular polygon = (Sum of interior angles) ÷ n

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dd98782cf4d30794ffa5a325ffb2555f9feef18e4331fe8faea5c7364399aff0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of **exterior angles** = 360°

⇒ Sum of **interior angles** = 360° + (200 ÷ 100) × 360°

⇒ Sum of **interior angles** = 360° + 720° = 1080°

⇒ (n − 2) × 180° = 1080°

⇒ n − 2 = 1080° ÷ 180°

⇒ n − 2 = 6

⇒ n = 8

⇒ Each **interior angle** (x) = 1080° ÷ 8

⇒ x = 135°

**∴ The correct answer is 135°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Interior and Exterior Angle Relation

For any vertex of a polygon, the **interior angle** and the **exterior angle** are supplementary, meaning their sum is always 180°.

Sum of Exterior Angles

The sum of the **exterior angles** of any convex polygon, regardless of the number of sides, is always 360°.

Number of Diagonals

The number of **diagonals** in a polygon with n sides is given by the formula: n(n − 3) ÷ 2.</p
